In the supplied simplified model, the aircraft drifts at 3 m/s during the link-loss delay and then travels the listed additional distance while braking. The limit is 20 meters total displacement from the loss point. Which profile meets that limit?

choices.A: Profile C only.
choices.B: Profile B only.
choices.C: Profile A only.

questions.explanation:
Correct: B. Profile B only.
B travels 3 x 3 = 9 meters during its delay, then 8 more while braking, totaling 17 meters. A totals 23 meters and C totals 22 meters. This checks only the stated model and limit.
Why A is incorrect: C's shorter delay produces 3 meters of drift, but its 19-meter braking travel makes the total 22 meters.
Why C is incorrect: A travels 3 x 5 + 8 = 23 meters, exceeding the 20-meter displacement limit.

questions.prompt:
Written scenario data: Adding a 1.0-kg payload gives: Aircraft A total mass 7 kg, available maximum thrust 8 kg-equivalent; Aircraft B total mass 7 kg, maximum thrust 10; Aircraft C total mass 8 kg, maximum thrust 9. Required unused thrust fraction is 25%.

A 1.0-kg payload will be added. The fictional policy requires at least 25 percent of maximum available thrust to remain unused in hover. Using the stated mass-equivalent model, which aircraft meets that requirement?

choices.A: Aircraft B only.
choices.B: Aircraft C only.
choices.C: Aircraft A only.

questions.explanation:
Correct: A. Aircraft B only.
B's new mass is 7 kg, requiring a 7-kg-equivalent hover thrust from 10 available. The unused fraction is (10 - 7)/10 = 30 percent, meeting the 25-percent policy.
Why B is incorrect: C's new mass is 8 kg against 9 kg-equivalent maximum thrust. Its unused fraction is 1/9, about 11.1 percent.
Why C is incorrect: A's new mass is 7 kg against 8 kg-equivalent maximum thrust. Its unused fraction is 1/8 = 12.5 percent.

questions.prompt: A monitor shows LIVE video, but the verified end-to-end delay is three seconds. The drone is approaching a narrow gap. What must the pilot account for?

choices.A: The word LIVE guarantees zero delay, so the gap can be judged only from the image.
choices.B: The displayed image depicts an earlier position, so immediate separation decisions need appropriate current references and a plan that accommodates the delay.
choices.C: Three seconds of delay improves obstacle clearance by making the drone physically slow down.

questions.explanation:

Live transmission can still have latency. The pilot must understand its age and avoid relying on a delayed image as a current separation measurement, while maintaining required VLOS.
Why A is incorrect: A live label does not establish zero latency.
Why C is incorrect: Transmission delay changes the information available to the pilot, not the aircraft's actual speed.

questions.prompt: A remote pilot completed the last qualifying knowledge event 25 calendar months ago and has flown only two hours since. No later qualifying event is on record. Can the low flight-hour total extend the Part 107 knowledge-recency window?
